assessment: This useful study, which systematically addresses off-target effects of a commonly used chemotherapy drug on bone and bone marrow cells and which therefore is of potential interest to a broad readership, presents evidence that reducing systemic inflammation induced by doxorubicin limits bone loss to some extent. The demonstration of the effect of systemic inflammation on bone loss is convincing. Building on prior work, this study sets the scene for additional genetic and pharmacologic experiments as well as future analyses of the bone phenotypes, which should speak to the mechanisms involved in doxorubicin-induced bone loss – which are not addressed in the current study – and which may substantiate the clinical relevance of targeting inflammation in order to limit the negative impact of chemotherapies on bone quality.
